verses.text: Joab son of Zeruiah could see that the king's heart longed for Absalom.

So Joab sent someone to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there. He said to her, "Please pretend to be in mourning. Put on mourning clothes and don't use any lotion. Act like a woman who has been mourning for someone who died a long time ago.
Then go to the king and say these words to him." And Joab told her exactly what to say.
The woman from Tekoa went to the king. She bowed down with her face to the ground to show respect and said, "Help me, my king!"
The king asked her, "What is the matter?" She answered, "I am a widow. My husband is dead.
I, your servant, had two sons. They got into a fight out in the field, and there was no one to separate them. One of them struck the other and killed him.

Now the whole family has turned against me, your servant. They say, 'Hand over the brother who killed his brother, so we can kill him for taking his brother's life. That way we will also get rid of the heir.' They want to put out the last spark of hope I have left. They would leave my husband with no name and no one to carry on his family on the earth."
The king said to the woman, "Go home, and I will give an order to protect you."
The woman from Tekoa said to the king, "My lord the king, let the blame fall on me and my father's family. Let the king and his throne be free of any blame."
The king said, "If anyone says anything to you, bring him to me, and he will never trouble you again."

Then she said, "Please, let the king call on the LORD your God, so that the relative who wants revenge will not kill any more and destroy my son." The king said, "As surely as the LORD lives, not one hair of your son's head will fall to the ground."
Then the woman said, "Please let your servant say one more thing to my lord the king." He said, "Go on."
The woman said, "Then why have you planned something like this against God's people? When you say this, you are judging yourself, because you have not brought home your own son whom you sent away.

All of us must die. We are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. But God does not just take away life. Instead, he makes ways for the person who was sent away not to stay cut off from him.
I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. I thought, 'I will speak to the king. Maybe he will do what I ask.'
Maybe the king will listen and rescue me from the man who wants to cut off both me and my son from the land God gave us.
And I thought, 'May the word of my lord the king give me peace.' For my lord the king is like an angel of God, able to tell good from bad. May the LORD your God be with you."
Then the king said to the woman, "Do not hide anything from me that I ask you." The woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."

The king asked, "Did Joab put you up to all this?" The woman answered, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything you say. Yes, it was your servant Joab who told me to do this. He put all these words in my mouth.
Your servant Joab did this to change the way things are. But my lord is as wise as an angel of God. You know everything that happens on earth."
Then the king said to Joab, "All right. I will do it. Go and bring back the young man Absalom."
Joab bowed down with his face to the ground to show respect, and he blessed the king. Joab said, "Today I know that you are pleased with me, my lord the king, because you have done what I asked."
Then Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.
But the king said, "He must go to his own house. He must not come to see me." So Absalom went to his own house and did not see the king.
In all Israel there was no man praised as much as Absalom for his good looks. From the bottom of his feet to the top of his head there was nothing wrong with him.

He cut his hair once a year, at the end of each year, because it became too heavy for him. When he weighed the hair he had cut, it weighed two hundred shekels by the royal standard, about two and a half kilograms.
Absalom had three sons and one daughter. His daughter's name was Tamar, and she was a beautiful woman.
Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two full years without seeing the king.
Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but Joab would not come to him. Absalom sent for him a second time, but he still would not come.
So Absalom said to his servants, "Look, Joab's field is next to mine, and he has barley growing there. Go and set it on fire." So Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
Then Joab went to Absalom's house and asked him, "Why did your servants set my field on fire?"

Absalom answered Joab, "I sent a message telling you to come here. I wanted to send you to the king to ask him, 'Why did I come back from Geshur? It would have been better for me to stay there.' Now let me see the king. If I am guilty of anything, let him put me to death."
So Joab went to the king and told him. Then the king called for Absalom, and he came and bowed down with his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.
